title: Renewal & expansion check-in — SummitCloud
summary: Check-in ahead of contract renewal. Customer wants reserve capacity increase for Q4 spikes, add EU region, discuss 12-month extension pricing and SOC2 artifacts. SE to run targeted latency/cost bench and propose Dedicated capacity + burst plan.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing for 12-month extension and capacity tiers (Sophie)
Liam to run targeted perf benchmark (p99 latency and tokens/sec) for SummitCloud workloads and share results (Liam)
Sophie to share SOC2 report and SSO/SAML integration guide (Sophie)
Schedule deep-dive with infra team for VPC/networking details next week (owner: Maya)
action_items: Sophie Park: Send updated 12-month pricing and proposed committed GPU pool tiers by 2026-07-10
Liam Chen: Run benchmark using customer prompt set and share spreadsheet link by 2026-07-12
Maya Patel: Share expected Q4 throughput numbers and peak concurrency by 2026-07-09
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Time: 09:30 PT
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO - SummitCloud), Carlos Ruiz (Platform Lead), Nina Gomez (Procurement)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh appreciate you taking the time. Quick agenda — renewal conversation, capacity needs for Q4, adding EU region, and then security artifacts. Sound good?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Maya): Yeah, that works. Thanks Sophie. We also want to cover timeline — we have budget planning next week so would help to nail down options.
00:32 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Got it. Liam, do you want to open on the technical side — what we saw from the usage and what capacity options look like?
00:40 Speaker 3 (Liam): Sure. So, um, quick summary: SummitCloud's usage has been steadily rising — token volume up about 2.7x YTD, and peak concurrency spikes around end-of-month invoices and Black Friday-ish test runs. Today you're on hosted API, correct? A couple of endpoints hitting p95 latencies in the 220–300ms range for 1-2k token prompts.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Maya): Yes hosted. We're seeing latency variance during spikes. The big ask from infra is predictable throughput for Q4. We're exploring dedicated capacity or reserved pools. Also need EU region for new customers there.
01:20 Speaker 3 (Liam): Right. Two recommended paths: 1) Redwood Dedicated — committed GPU pool with autoscale and burst, gives predictable throughput and capacity isolation; or 2) keep hosted and add provisioned reserved concurrency with higher tier SLA. Trade-offs are cost vs max predictability.
01:36 Speaker 4 (Carlos): Can you quantify the cost delta? Our finance team will need ballpark for committed vs on-demand.
01:44 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We'll send formal pricing but ballpark — committed Dedicated pools reduce per-token cost by ~25–40% depending on utilization compared to hosted on-demand. There's also a monthly commit component. We'll include a few tiers.
01:58 Speaker 3 (Liam): For performance, we recommend running a targeted benchmark with your production prompt set — p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. I can run the benchmark on a 4-GPU pool and a 16-GPU pool to show linear scaling and tail latency differences.
02:14 Speaker 2 (Maya): That would be great. Also, in EU we need data residency — logs and key material must stay in region. Do you support EU-only data storage for private customers?
02:27 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Yes. For Dedicated we can provision region-specific pools and for Private deployments there's full control. For hosted we have EU regions with data residency options, and we can show the KMS integration and audit logs. We'll attach SOC2 and our region data policy.
02:42 Speaker 4 (Nina): On procurement — contract extension length impacts discount. If we go 12 months with a commit, procurement is looking for price protection and SLAs on throughput.
02:53 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Understood. We typically offer step discounts for 12–24 month terms, and SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated. I'll include a 12-month proposal with a burst capacity clause and an option to add a third region at a pre-negotiated rate.
03:06 Speaker 3 (Liam): A quick technical clarification — you mentioned KV cache earlier in your notes; just so we're aligned, we use prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost on repeated prompts. There might be mis-transcription in some docs where "KV" got recorded as "K-V" or something.
03:20 Speaker 2 (Maya): Yeah we've seen some oddness in the notes. One question — do we have an option to do a hybrid: Dedicated for US + hosted EU for initial launch? That would let us defer commitment in EU until demand grows.
03:33 Speaker 3 (Liam): Absolutely. Hybrid routing is supported — policy can route EU traffic to EU hosted region and US traffic to Dedicated pool. We can set fallbacks to reduce outage risk.
03:44 Speaker 4 (Carlos): In terms of networking, for Dedicated we need to confirm VPC peering and egress rules. Also, does Dedicated support customer-managed KMS?
03:55 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Yes on both. We'll provide the VPC/VPN and KMS integration docs. For on-prem/private installs we support HSM integrations as well.
04:07 Speaker 2 (Maya): Okay. Next: benchmarks. If Liam runs benchmarks, can you use our real prompt set and the sample dataset we uploaded?
04:15 Speaker 3 (Liam): Yep — if you share the set and the typical concurrency profile (requests per second, tokens per req), I'll run both throughput and tail latency tests and post a spreadsheet. I'll also include quantized model variants if you want to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
04:29 Speaker 2 (Maya): We do want that. Also, security: we need SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO/SAML integration guide, and audit logs retention policy.
04:40 Speaker 1 (Sophie): I'll email SOC2 and SSO docs after the call. We have standard retention options (30/90/365 days) for logs; for Dedicated/Private you can choose retention longer and export logs to your SIEM.
04:53 Speaker 4 (Nina): Procurement: will you add a clause for service credits if p99 latency exceeds X? We need measurable remedies.
05:00 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We can include a p99 latency SLO for critical endpoints as an optional add-on. For Dedicated we can be quite prescriptive. I'll draft language for review.
05:10 Speaker 2 (Maya): Timeline — we need final numbers by 7/12 for budget planning. Can you commit to providing pricing and the benchmark by then?
05:19 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Yes. I'll put pricing on 7/10, Liam will deliver benchmark by 7/12, and we'll schedule follow-up deep-dive for VPC details next week.
05:32 Speaker 3 (Carlos): One more thing — competitors: some teams are evaluating Anthropic and Vertex for multi-region latency. How do you see Redwood positioned?
05:42 Speaker 1 (Sophie): We focus on production-first serving and cost controls: autoscaling, KV caching, and routing policies. We'll highlight unit economics vs Anthropic hosted and ease of Dedicated deployment vs building in-house.
05:56 Speaker 2 (Maya): Perfect. Anything else?
06:00 Speaker 1 (Sophie): Quick recap and next steps: Sophie sends pricing and SOC2 + SSO docs, Liam runs benchmarks, Maya shares Q4 throughput numbers, and we meet again for VPC deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
06:12 Speaker 2 (Maya): Thanks, appreciate it.

Notes / links shared during call:
- Pricing deck link: https://redwood.ai/decks/q3-capacity-pricing (shared)
- Benchmark sheet (placeholder): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/summitcloud-q3 (Liam will populate)
- SOC2 & SSO guide: Sophie to attach in follow-up

End of transcript.
